Mahmoud Abuwarda (born 1990) is a Palestinian composer, classical guitarist, and music educator. His work blends symphonic, cinematic, and contemporary elements, often integrating traditional Arabic music with Western classical forms.  His compositions have been performed internationally in the United States, Middle East and Europe.
Early Life and Education
Born in Gaza in 1990, Abuwarda received his early musical training in classical guitar at the Edward Said National Conservatory of Music (ESNCM) – Birzeit University in Palestine, studying under guitarist Pedro López de La Osa. He later pursued advanced studies in music theory and composition through Berklee Online, supported by the Gary Burton Scholarship.
Career
Between 2012 and 2022, Abuwarda held multiple academic and administrative positions at the Edward Said National Conservatory of Music, including professor of composition, guitar instructor, music theory teacher, academic supervisor, and head of the guitar department. He has also taught at Zemas College in Istanbul.
Since relocating to Turkey, Abuwarda has continued his academic and pedagogical career. He co-founded the Istanbul Intercultural Conservatory of Music, where he serves as the academic director, and also holds a teaching position at the Rumeli International College.
Beyond his academic roles, Abuwarda served as the director of the "Sea and Freedom" Music Festival in Palestine. He has also been featured as a guest at international arts events, including the Lisbon & Sintra Film Festival (LEFFEST) in Portugal.
In August 2025, Abuwarda's orchestral piece "A Story to Tell " received its world premiere in Portugal.  The performance, executed by the Orquestra Sinfonietta de Lisboa, served as the opening symphonic concert for the Festa do Avante! festival. Although visa restrictions prevented Abuwarda from attending physically, the event highlighted themes of peace and solidarity with Palestine, presenting his music to a European audience.
Abuwarda is a member of the Dahaleez Collective, contributing to contemporary sound installations featured at the OTO Sound Museum. The museum's permanent collection also includes his orchestral composition, "A Story to Tell "
In April 2026, Abuwarda was announced as a winner of the JERUS-IT-ARTS International Contest, a European initiative focused on intercultural dialogue between Italy and Jerusalem.
Furthermore, Abuwarda's music has been featured in European cultural events advocating for human rights. In Italy, his work was included during the "Nessun Dorma" solidarity event in Civitanova Alta.
Pedagogical Works and Intercultural Dialogue
Abuwarda has demonstrated a strong commitment to music education and cross-cultural dialogue through his published works. He collaborated with American-Jewish piano educator [https://www.pennylazaruspianostudio.com/home Penny Lazarus] to create the piano collection "Scenes from Palestinian Childhood". Conceived as a message of peace, the book serves as a pedagogical resource that introduces students to Middle Eastern musical elements. Notably, the collection features a composition that harmonically integrates traditional Palestinian and Jewish folk melodies, symbolizing intercultural harmony.
In April 2026, this collaborative book and Abuwarda's pedagogical approach were featured in a bilingual (Arabic and English) study in the [https://www.mtnaejournal.org/ MTNA e-Journal]. The article, authored by Vanessa Cornett, Nationally Certified Teacher of Music NCTM, and Salam Murtada, highlighted the collection as a significant tool for piano instruction, specifically for teaching children, and provided a detailed musical analysis of his other works, including "Dream of a Quiet Sky" and "Reflections in Turmoil".
Furthermore, Abuwarda's expertise in Middle Eastern musical traditions has led to international academic invitations. He was invited by the University of Oklahoma to deliver guest lectures on World Music and rhythmic structures in Oriental music. His growing academic and artistic profile, bridging Eastern and Western musical identities, has been highlighted by major European media outlets, including Italian television.
Performances and Collaborations
Abuwarda's works encompass orchestral, chamber, and solo pieces. His piece "A Distant Lament " was performed in the Old City of Jerusalem, as well as at cultural venues in Italy.
In Europe, his compositions have been performed through collaborations with academic institutions and international artists. The Conservatorio di Vicenza in Italy hosted a concert featuring his works that integrate Eastern and Western musical traditions.  His piano compositions, specifically the Nocturnes, have been recorded by Italian pianist Alberto Nones and featured on the Fazioli Pianos artist platform. In 2025, his piece "Nocturne No, 2 - Notturno di Gaza" premiered at the Montecassiano Music Festival in Italy, also performed by Nones.
Furthermore, two of Abuwarda's compositions received their world premiere recordings by Italian pianist Alberto Nones: the solo piano nocturne "Stars Over the Sleeping City", which conceptually evokes the final night of peace in Gaza, and "Fragments of Memory Falling", a duet for cello and piano.
Additionally, his orchestral work "A Story to Tell " was performed by the Orquestra Sinfonietta de Lisboa at the Festa do Avante! festival in Seixal, Portugal. In the United Kingdom, his composition "A Voice From Afar " was performed by the duet Cellocroí and received critical coverage in Buzz Magazine.
Expanding into multimedia and visual arts, Abuwarda composed the music for the virtual project "Sahab Museum" in collaboration with the Hawaf collective, which was featured at the international [https://www.artexplora.org/en/festival Art Explora Festival].
In April 2026, Abuwarda collaborated with Italian pianist and musicologist Alberto Nones to compose Nocturne No. 6: Nothing or Something. The piece was dedicated to the memory of his late student, Lubna Alyaan, who was killed in Gaza. Recorded in Pesaro, Italy, the production featured prominent Italian musicians, including baritone Gabriele Spina, violinist Marco Santini, and the Giardino delle Voci children's choir. The composition, characterized by its multicultural elements featuring lyrics in Arabic, English, and Italian, was slated for release by the prominent Italian label Halidon Music, alongside a collection of Abuwarda's solo piano nocturnes.
Compositions
Abuwarda's musical catalog encompasses orchestral works, chamber music, keyboard pieces, and solo instrumental compositions, which are registered with Broadcast Music, Inc. (BMI).
In 2026, Abuwarda's cello duet "A Voice From Afar " was performed by the cello duet Cellocroí. The work, reflecting on themes of separation and resilience, received critical attention; a review in Buzz Magazine described its "melancholy notes" as being anchored by the composer's gratitude and enduring hope.
